messages:
Maya Li: Ran an nsys trace on the fp8/INT8 hybrid build with the new batching slew heuristic. attaching quick summary + trace link. deconv kernel time is spiking under certain batch mixes. :thinking:

Devin K: link: https://internal-traces/redwood/1853101112/heatmap (nsys TL) :eyes:

Maya Li: TL;DR from the trace: when batch mix has many short requests + a few long ones the scheduler picks the deconv_no_win kernel variant which has ~6.0-7.5ms latency vs deconv_win ~2.8-3.5ms. dequant kernel is ~0.9-1.3ms per call, but it runs more often due to prefix KV behavior.

Sasha: repro steps? which config and model size?

Maya Li: repro: model=gptx-13b-fp8-int8, hw=A100-80GB, seq=1024, request dist: 80% seq<=64, 20% seq~512. runtime flags: --batch-slew=adaptive, --kv-cache=shared-prefix, quant-mode=hybrid. nsys cmd: ```nsys profile -o /tmp/1853 --trace=cuda,cudnn --sample=none --capture-range=cudaKernelLaunch --force-overwrite --stats true --app-name "serve" -- ./serve --config ...```

Devin K: interesting. batching slew tries to combine short requests into a single launch but keeps long ones separate. Seems kernel selector chooses no_win for combined launches because it assumes no persistent workspace; probably due to memory plan mismatch when KV cache spill occurs.

Maya Li: exact kernel timeline excerpt (copied):
```
[ts+0.000] deconv_no_win <<<grid>>>    6.21ms  1.2MB
[ts+6.221] dequant_wide           1.02ms  0.0MB
[ts+7.243] kv_load_prefix         0.45ms
[ts+7.700] deconv_no_win          6.32ms
[ts+13.99] dequant_wide          1.08ms
[ts+15.08] hostsync              0.60ms
```

Sasha: so we pay ~13ms for two deconv_no_win launches + dequant overhead ~2.1ms -> ~15ms token chunk. If we get deconv_win we would be ~7ms total. that explains tokens/sec drop.

perf-bot: perf-regression-check: compared to baseline (fixed-batch=64, KV pinned) we see -42% throughput for mixed short/long workload. Threshold exceeded. :warning:

Maya Li: hypothesis A: kernel selector cost model uses peak_workspace estimate which is inflated when KV shared-prefix is active, pushing it to choose no_win. Hypothesis B: batching slew packs requests in a way that violates alignment that deconv_win requires.

Devin K: quick experiment I ran: forced selector to prefer win-variant via env SELECTOR_PREFER=win -> throughput up +35% on mixed workload, but memory faults in very long sequences (seq=2048) for some runs. So safe only with KV warmup/pinning.

Ops-Alex: ops notes: we saw a few OOMs on dedicated infra when forcing win kernel at peak. might need guard rails.

Maya Li: next actions I propose:
- Add a lightweight check in selector: if kv_cache_shared and batch_mix_has_long-> prefer no_win only if peak_workspace > threshold. else prefer win.
- Add runtime flag --force-kernel-variant for canary testing.
- Measure dequant call frequency: if dequant invocations per token > 0.6 -> consider fusing dequant into deconv path for hot-path.

Devin K: +1. Also we should try changing batching heuristic to avoid combining very short requests with a long one (split groups by seq length bucketing). simple fix: bucket at 128. quick perf win.

Sasha: can I take the dequant-invocation profile? where do you dump the counters?

Maya Li: counters are in /var/log/serve/prof/counters.json in trace runs (counter keys: dequant_calls, deconv_launches, kv_loads). I exported one for this run -> dequant_calls=1823, deconv_launches=342, kv_loads=1980. dequant_calls / deconv_launches ~5.3 -> we are calling dequant often (many small fragments).

Devin K: sounds like fusing or caching dequant results per token prefix could help. but need accuracy check: fused quant path changes rounding order, run eval on our prompts.

Maya Li: ran quality eval on 500 prompt set: delta_ROUGE ~0.2% vs baseline int8-only -> acceptable for canary.

perf-bot: scheduling follow-up: create ticket PERF-3857 with logs + selectors + trace link.

Maya Li: I'll open PERF-3857 and attach this trace + the forced-selector run. assigning to @Devin K and @Sasha. thanks all. :thumbsup:
